name: Ui_Tween_EvalModeC8Only
summary: Parameter evaluator: when the track's mode byte +0xC is 8 it returns sample(0x325BDC) + track->f_0, otherwise it returns track->f_0 unchanged, i.e. the parameter only animates for mode 8.
evidence: NEW: the table at 0x7286A0 is a real array of 60 {fnptr, this_adjust} entries (asm/rodata/rodata_00725000.s; entry 24 = 0x325FEC, entry 0 = 0x3267C0) and the dispatcher 0x326428 tail-calls table[row->f_28] after checking row->f_29 against the requested parameter id, returning track->f_0 when the row does not match. name: maybe_Ui_SlotWindow_UpdateSubWidget
summary: Slot-window refresh entry: forwards the tick at self+0x56C to the embedded widget at +0x588 (Ui_Widget_Update), then drives the payout state machine - resets the payout animation, requests state 0x10/0x11 depending on the +0x48 flag, notifies the widget at self->f_14 and restores the default float pair.
evidence: NEW: all 11 callers are now named and all belong to the slot machine (Ui_SlotWindow_AnimCallbackB/E, Ui_SlotWindow_UpdateIdleState, Ui_SlotWindow_SetReelState, Ui_SlotWindow_PayoutSequence, Casino_Slot_ApplyBetAndPayout/StopReel/ExecCommand, Ui_SlotMachine_UpdateInput), so the class is settled. The method role is not: the readable body is only halt_baddata and the disassembly shows widget update + payout reset + two state requests, so 'UpdateSubWidget' names only the first third of it. Kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_TwoListPanel_Ctor
summary: In-place constructor of a two-list window variant: runs the window header constructor (0x1D08D8), installs the class vtable 0x763E68 plus the secondary table at +0x4C, then constructs the two embedded sub-objects (vtables 0x767258 and 0x75ECE0) and clears their state words.
evidence: NEW: the literal at 0x329D54 is 0x00763E68, and that vtable carries the named Ui_TwoListWindow_Init (0x329AFC, slot 0x20) and Ui_TwoListWindow_UpdateChildSelection (0x329A8C, slot 0x18), so the class is a two-list window variant - the old 'Panel' wording is at least in the right family. It is a subclass though (slots 0/1 are its own dtor 0x329DB4 / 0x329D60), and the two embedded objects use the emotion-balloon (0x767258) and pane-group (0x75ECE0) vtables, so the exact subclass name is still open. Kept maybe_.

name: Dive_Effect_InitFromActor
summary: Initialises one dive-effect parameter from the owning actor: takes the actor's visual/monster id (self->f_28->f_238), looks it up in the lazily built shared table (0x63E5C8) and stores tableRow->f_E2 (a size/rate byte) scaled by a constant into self->f_A0; id -1 keeps the default.
evidence: NEW: the method table at 0x7254B8 holds this function next to the already-named Dive_SpawnDropEffect (0x32AC88) and maybe_Gfx_SpawnScreenShake (0x32ABE0), so the Dive_ class prefix is no longer a guess; the body's only work is the id -> f_E2 lookup and the scaled store into f_A0, which is exactly 'init from actor'.

name: Dive_Effect_UpdateStartDelay
summary: Per-frame start-delay check of the dive effect: while the frame counter f_38 is not yet 0x3C (60) it does nothing; on frame 60 it asks the tween controller at +0x2C for state 2 and commits it, i.e. the effect starts. Always returns 1 so the caller keeps ticking.
evidence: NEW: the method table at 0x7254F0 holds it next to maybe_Ui_DiveEffect_Update (0x32A850), so the class is the dive effect. The old name 'UpdateTimer' was wrong: the body never increments anything - it only tests `self->f_38 == 0x3C` and then runs the request/commit pair (vtable+0x14(2) then vtable+0x10), so the function is the delayed-start gate, not a timer update.

name: maybe_Dive_Effect_SpawnOriented
summary: Spawns effect 0x45C on an actor with a fully built 0x60-byte instance parameter block: copies the actor transform from actor+0x28->0x9C, builds and orthonormalises a second basis from two global vectors, applies the left/right mirror flags and hands the block to Effect_FindOrCreateInstance.
evidence: NEW: nothing changed the verdict - there is still no readable C for this address (only the instruction-listing pseudo-C in decomp/functions/maybe_Gfx_SpawnScreenShakeAlt.c), and the address is not referenced from any rodata table. The R_062 disassembly reading (vsqrt/vdiv basis maths, vneg mirror fixes, Effect_FindOrCreateInstance with effect id 0x45C from the literal at 0x32B3D8, single caller the dive-effect spawner at 0x32B04C) is the only evidence, and it fixes the behaviour but not the class name. Kept maybe_.

name: maybe_TweenSequence_Update
summary: Three-step animation timeline: accumulates the frame delta into f_34/f_38, then runs the callback of the current step (0..2) from the 0x18-byte descriptor array at +0x2C, resolving the (fn & 1) thunk convention against the object at +0x4C.
evidence: NEW: the function is slot 0 of the table at 0x764060, whose preceding entries are 0x32B618, maybe_Model_HandleDeadTag (0x32A6D0) and 0x32B48C - i.e. model/effect code, not UI. The old 'Ui_' prefix is therefore not supported and is dropped; the timeline body itself (3-step descriptor array, thunk resolution) is unchanged and still matches Field_NpcAction_UpdateTimeline 0x32FBB4. The class is still open, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveManager_Update
summary: Per-frame update of the dive manager: asks the virtual state query (vtable+0xC) whether it is idle; when it is not, a successful condition check sets the 'ready' byte at +0x18; when it is, four pending sub-objects are released through their vtable+8 and their flags cleared.
evidence: NEW: the vtable at 0x7641B8 starts with Ui_DiveManager_Dtor (0x32C92C) and Ui_DiveManager_DeletingDtor (0x32C91C) and this function is slot 2 of that same table, so the class is Ui_DiveManager - the old 'DiveResultWindow' wording named a different class. The method role (idle query + release of four pending sub-objects) is visible, but the body is partly damaged (self[2]/self[5] indexing), so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_DamagePopup_DetachActor
summary: Tests the popup's actor link at f_28 and, when it resolves, calls 0x5E7848(actor, 0, 1) - the same call the sibling 0x322884 makes with flag 0, so this is the 'detach / clear the actor link' variant.
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x764240 is confirmed as the battle damage class - slot 0 is maybe_Battle_DamagePopup_DeletingDestructor (0x32CCB4), slot 1 maybe_Battle_Damage_PlayAnimAndSe (0x32CBF8) and this function is slot 3. The class is settled, but 0x5E7848 is still unnamed, so what the call actually does to the actor (detach vs. reset) is inferred. Kept maybe_.

name: Battle_DamagePopup_DeletingDestructor
summary: Deleting destructor of the battle damage popup: tears down its string/member (0x193E44) and frees the object (0x10F6CC).
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x764240 has this function in slot 0 and its other slots are the named maybe_Battle_Damage_PlayAnimAndSe (0x32CBF8) and maybe_Battle_DamagePopup_DetachActor (0x32CC54), so the class is confirmed by its own vtable rather than by the body alone; the body is the standard 'member teardown + free' pair.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_DeletingDestructor
summary: Deleting destructor of a field actor/scene-node class: releases the base object (0x5F8528) and frees it (0x10F6CC).
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x7642DC has this function in slot 0 and its other slots are Field_Actor_ReleaseAttachedEffect (0x32DA9C), maybe_Field_SceneNode_ResetChildren (0x32D264) and Field_Actor_RestartActionSequence (0x32D998) plus the 0x5F7xxx Gfx node methods - so the old 'Gfx_Sprite' class was wrong, this is a field actor. Which of Field_Actor / Field_SceneNode owns the vtable is not settled (both names appear as siblings), so the name stays maybe_.

name: Field_Actor_TickEffectState
summary: Per-frame effect-state tick: once the accumulated timer at actor->f_4C+8 passes 0.3 (0x3E99999A) it spawns the state effect once (0x32DE54, guarded by f_230) and then asks the sub-state at f_4C for state 2. Always returns 1.
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x764454 has this function in slot 0 with maybe_Field_Actor_BeginEffectState (0x32DBEC) as the preceding entry, so the Field_Actor class is confirmed by its own vtable; the body's two steps (spawn once, then request state 2) are visible in the readable C.

name: maybe_Gfx_Node_StartAnim
summary: Starts the node animation: installs the per-frame callback &LAB_0032de44 through vtable+0x84, starts an animation of length 0x3C through 0x5F7784, sets the running byte f_8C and clears the byte at +0x221.
evidence: NEW: the callee 0x5F7784 belongs to the same 0x5F7xxx family as the named Gfx_Node_DrawModel (0x5F7578), so the class is a Gfx node, not specifically a sprite - the old 'Gfx_Sprite' wording is dropped. The function is not referenced from any rodata table and has no static caller, so the exact node class and the meaning of the 0x3C length are still open. Kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_DeletingDestructor
summary: Deleting destructor of a second field scene-node class: releases the base object (0x5F8528) and frees it (0x10F6CC) - same body as 0x32DBD0.
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x764394 has this function in slot 0 and its other slots are maybe_Field_SceneNode_CreateChild_75AEB8 (0x3D5E58) and Field_Actor_UpdateVisibility (0x3D6064) plus the 0x5F7xxx Gfx node methods, so the old 'Gfx_Sprite' class was wrong. The vtable mixes Field_SceneNode_* and Field_Actor_* siblings, so which of the two owns it is not settled; kept maybe_ and named after the scene-node side to stay distinct from 0x32DBD0.

name: Field_NpcAction_UpdateTimeline
summary: Per-frame NPC-action timeline: accumulates the delta into f_68/f_6C and then runs the callback of the current keyframe (0..11) from the 0x18-byte descriptor array at +0x60, resolving the (fn & 1) thunk convention against the object at +0x80.
evidence: NEW: the callback table at 0x764838 holds this function together with Field_NpcAction_AdvanceTweenState (0x330F08), and the vtable right after it (0x76484C) is the Field_NpcAction_RunToLink class with RunToLinkSetup/RunToLinkUpdate - so the Field_NpcAction base class is confirmed by named siblings. The timeline body is unchanged; only the jump table inside it is unrecovered.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteSlot_SetParams
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SpriteSlot_SetParams(u32 index, u8 flagA, u8 flagB)
summary: Fills one 0x40-byte entry of a global sprite/effect parameter array: copies three words of the default basis vector into +0x48/+0x4C/+0x50 and stores the caller's flags in the trailing bytes +0x54..+0x58.
evidence: NEW: nothing new - the address is not referenced from any rodata table and has no static caller, and Ghidra's body is still damaged (coprocessor_function, 'index' used as a pointer), so the base register and the array owner remain guesses. Only the 0x40 stride and the three-word copy are confirmed by the instruction listing. A confident name here would be inventing.

name: Field_NpcAction_StartAnimAndFlagStep
summary: Starts the action's animation through the actor's vtable+0x84 (callback 0x3308E8) and, when the action counter f_2C8 is below 4, sets the matching 'step done' byte in the array at self->f_5C (+0x271 + counter).
evidence: NEW: the method table at 0x7257DC holds this function next to the named Field_NpcAction_WaitForLinkEnd (0x330DF0), so the Field_NpcAction class is confirmed by named siblings; the body's two steps (vtable+0x84 animation start, then the guarded step-done byte) are visible in the recovered fragment.

name: Field_NpcAction_AdvanceTweenState
summary: Asks the action's tween controller at +0x60 whether the current step finished (vtable+0x14 with no id) and, if it did, commits the next state through vtable+0x10.
evidence: NEW: the callback table at 0x764838 pairs this function with Field_NpcAction_UpdateTimeline (0x32FBB4), which drives the same +0x60 controller, and the neighbouring vtable 0x76484C is the named Field_NpcAction_RunToLink class - so the Field_NpcAction base class is confirmed. The request/commit pair is the same two-slot protocol as the named message-window tween code (0x30E3CC).

name: Field_NpcAction_RunToLink_DeletingDestructor
summary: Deleting destructor of the 'run to link' NPC action: destroys the string member (0x193E40) and frees the object (0x10F6CC).
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x76484C has this function in slot 0 and the named Field_NpcAction_RunToLinkSetup (0x3314B0, slot 1) and Field_NpcAction_RunToLinkUpdate (0x33164C, slot 3) as its other entries, so the class is the run-to-link action - the old name 'DeletingDestructorB' did not identify the class at all.

name: Field_NpcJumpAction_DeletingDestructor
summary: Deleting destructor of the NPC jump action: destroys the string member (0x193E40) and frees the object (0x10F6CC).
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x764880 has this function in slot 0 and the named Field_NpcJumpAction_Setup (0x3317B8, slot 1) and Field_NpcJumpAction_Update (0x331B74, slot 3) as its other entries, so the class is confirmed by its own vtable.

name: Field_NpcAction_RunToward_DeletingDestructor
summary: Deleting destructor of the 'run toward target' NPC action: destroys the string member (0x193E40) and frees the object (0x10F6CC).
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x7648B4 has this function in slot 0 and the named Field_NpcAction_RunTowardTargetStart (0x331DAC, slot 1) and Field_NpcAction_RunTowardTargetUpdate (0x331E04, slot 3) as its other entries, so the class is confirmed by its own vtable.

name: maybe_Actor_OnStateExit
summary: State-exit hook: refreshes the actor's level-grid revision (0x179084 on self->f_28) and clears the actor's pending action id at +0x2A8.
evidence: NEW: the vtable 0x76491C has this function in slot 2, right after Field_NpcAction_SubactionDeletingDtor (0x332E58) and next to maybe_Actor_OnStateChanged (0x332DCC, slot 6), so it is a state hook of that class. The old name 'StopStateAnim' was wrong - the body does no animation work at all, it only refreshes the grid and clears the action id. The exact hook (enter vs. exit) is still inferred, so it stays maybe_.

name: Err_ThrowFatalErrorWithCode
summary: Builds a 0xF80-byte nn::err FatalErrInfo on the stack, tags its first word with 2, runs the two err:f state helpers (0x51CCF8 / 0x51CD28) and launches the fatal-error applet (0x51CC68).
evidence: NEW: every callee is the nn::err fatal-error applet - Err_FatalErrInfo_Init (0x51CBF8), Err_LaunchFatalErrorApplet (0x51CC68) and Err_ThrowFatalError (0x51CCFC), and FACTS.md pins 0x51BA34..0x51CD40 as CTR SDK nn::err. The old name 'Sound_InitChannelWork' was wrong: the 0xF80-byte block is a FatalErrInfo, not a sound channel-work block, and nothing here touches the sound driver.
